rationale: C03 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child’s tax-refund veto. Both describe taxes whose treatment differed among similarly situated taxpayers, reject selective retroactive relief, and use the distinctive concern that refunding taxes may create a windfall because the nominal taxpayer may not have borne the tax burden. C01 and C18 share the tax-administration, judicial-clarification, discrimination, and veto-closing structure, but their principal machinery concerns untimely refund claims and statutes of limitation, which are absent from the child.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the bill might unjustly enrich its beneficiaries by refunding the cabaret tax without regard to whether the ultimate burden of the tax was borne by the claimants or passed on to their patrons
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the burden of British tax may not rest on United States licensors in such cases. Consequently, to allow the British tax as a credit against the United States tax on a retroactive basis would give a windfall gain to some American licensors
shared_material.explanation: This is a distinctive shared burden-shifting and windfall rationale, adapted from royalties to cabaret taxes.

shared_material.child_excerpt: similarly situated taxpayers in many States were not required to pay the tax... [the bill] would also discriminate against many other similarly situated taxpayers
shared_material.parent_excerpt: produce a different combination of British and United States taxes on the royalties paid some American recipients than on others... The proposed change would single out for special relief a small group of taxpayers
shared_material.explanation: Both move from nonuniform tax treatment to rejection of legislation benefiting only a selected taxpayer group.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The bill would direct the Secretary of the Treasury to pay... in refund of cabaret taxes... Under the circumstances, therefore, I am constrained to withhold my approval of the bill.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This bill would extend... a credit for taxes... For these reasons, I am constrained to withhold my approval of the bill.
shared_material.explanation: The shared operative structure presents retroactive tax relief, analyzes unequal treatment and windfall effects, and closes by withholding approval.
